_comment:
ADR-app-0002 SS 0/2: every module carries exactly one "kind", and it is the ONLY per-module presentation fact in this file - the picker's grouping, its group headings, the muted treatment and the "kein Nachweis" marker on comparison modules are all derived from it in app.js (see MODULE_KIND_GROUPS / renderModulePicker there). Adding a second hand-written per-module presentation string is the thing this field exists to prevent: the picker was designed for a handful of modules, now lists 29, and any per-module copy would have to be written and translated 29 times and would go stale the way the hand-maintained locale claims did.
  licence    - a real state exam exists elsewhere; we are exam prep for it.
  compliance - no official exam anywhere; our completion record IS the proof.
  cert       - an external professional exam exists (IHK/HWK, CNCF).
  compare    - confers nothing anywhere; another jurisdiction's rules as a comparison object.
DELIBERATELY NOT the same field as the KB's module_kind (exam_prep / compliance / fun_translation / ui_strings, data-rules.md SS 3). That one is a LICENSING and AUTHORING fact - it decides what a content round may source from and how it must be identified. This one is a PRESENTATION fact - it decides what a row looks like in one dialog. They agree today on most modules and would still have to be maintained apart: aevo and cka are both module_kind "exam_prep" like fuehrerschein, but a learner sorting 29 rows needs them separated from the state-exam set, and a future presentation split (or a KB kind with no picker consequence) must not force a re-licensing review. Merging them would couple a legal decision to a layout one.

modules._comment: 2026-08-17: the German Ausbildereignungspruefung under the Ausbilder-Eignungsverordnung (AusbEignV 2009 vom 21.1.2009, BGBl. I S. 88), grounded in BBiG §§ 27-30. Same regulation and same BIBB Rahmenplan whether the administering chamber is an IHK or an HWK - only the certifying chamber differs. This module is PRACTICE-EXAM framed, not a light concept check: unlike CKA (whose real exam is 100 % hands-on, making a concept check the honest choice there), the AEVO's written part genuinely is a 180-minute closed-form multiple-choice exam with 80 fallbezogene Aufgaben across all four Handlungsfelder (§ 4 Abs. 2 AEVO plus the chambers' Merkblaetter). 76-question DE/EN pilot; four topics mapping 1:1 onto the four Handlungsfelder of § 2 AEVO, weighted per the current Rahmenplan (Empfehlung des BIBB-Hauptausschusses vom 20.6.2023, BAnz AT 14.07.2023 S2) at 15/20/50/15 % rather than evenly - see data/gen_aevo.py's META.topic_weighting_note for the caveat that this is a Lehrgangsdauer recommendation, not a published exam question-count distribution. hasCourse: the course layer carries the PRACTICAL exam part (§ 4 Abs. 3 AEVO - presentation or live delivery of a training situation plus a Fachgespraech) as written, NON-QUIZZED guidance, because a performance task cannot honestly be tested as MCQ. Ships free, like every module in this app today - pricing remains intentionally deferred. AI-drafted, NOT legally reviewed, and explicitly unofficial: there is no official public AEVO question catalogue, so this pool cannot claim to cover the real exam - see the pilot's legal_review_status.

Another country's road rules, carried as a curiosity and comparison object next to the German Fuehrerschein module - NOT German exam preparation and NOT that jurisdiction's official exam. 50 questions, DE/EN only (fun_translation modules sit outside the 15-locale set and must never be counted as locale-coverage gaps). Questions were authored from California Vehicle Code (CVC) — the statute itself, all 50 questions: the primary law, never from a driver handbook - a handbook is a compiled authored work and translating one would be a derivative of the whole thing (§ 3b again; a handbook may be read for topic COVERAGE, never for text).
